overview.training.name: Training Dataset
point.title: Decision: train per cell not per car
point.lede: 10 cars to sample is a very small dataset, so it needs to be made larger. Still need to hold out by car to train to avoid memorization/nearest neighbor issues.
point.cars.caption: Per car
point.cells.caption: Per cell
inputs.title: Hand-roll ‘embeddings’
inputs.lede: 10 examples don’t work for a PointNet-style embedding network for the 16-hyperparameter design space, but we can compute our own
inputs.notes.position: Four distances (m): from the nose, to the tail, out from the center plane and up from the lowest point. And the three surface normal components.
inputs.notes.surface: Geometry/surface around the cell at 4 different distances. Average surface normals, areas.
inputs.notes.slices: Thirteen slices across the body, each twice as far from the cell as the last, so nearby shape is read in detail and distant shape in bulk. From each slice: its area, and how far it reaches outboard of, above and below the cell's position (the hollow mark). A reach is negative where the slice stops short of that position.
inputs.notes.all: Each number is centred and scaled by its values over the training cells. All {inputs} go into {networksWord} networks, and the prediction is their mean.
inputs.key: Brown = below mean, white = at mean, blue = above mean
inputs.car.caption: The same, on {car}
inputs.car.hint: Drag the cell, or tap anywhere on the car
networks.title: {NetworksWord} networks
networks.lede: Each network trains on {trainedOnWord} of the cars and is scored on the other {heldOutWord}. The split is by whole car. Neighbouring cells on one car are nearly identical, so a random split of cells would score a network on cars it trained on.
networks.network.caption: One network, at this cell
networks.folds.caption: Cars each network trained on
networks.folds.name: Network {network}
networks.learners.caption: Other models on the same inputs, cross-validated R²
accuracy.title: Prediction against CFD
accuracy.headlines.crossValidation: R² on the {trainingCars} training cars, each predicted by the network that did not train on it
accuracy.headlines.outside.one: R², DrivAerML run {runs}, kept out of training
accuracy.headlines.outside.other: R², DrivAerML runs {runs}, kept out of training
accuracy.missing: {car} has no CFD pressure, so there is no error to show.
accuracy.scatter.caption: Every cell, predicted against CFD, weighted by area
accuracy.regions.caption: Mean error by region, and each region's share of the surface
spread.title: Spread: where the networks disagree
spread.lede: The spread is the standard deviation of the {networksWord} networks' answers at a cell, scaled so that on the training cars it is the size of the error.
spread.missing: {car} has no CFD pressure, so its spread cannot be compared with its error.
spread.calibration.caption: Error against spread, cells grouped by spread
spread.headlines.car: of this car's surface has an error within the spread
spread.headlines.outside: of the surface on the runs kept out of training
drag.title: Pressure drag
drag.lede: Pressure drag is the predicted pressure summed over the car. In cross-validation it is off by {model} counts on average; guessing the training cars' average is off by {average}. Drag is the small difference between two larger sums, over the surfaces facing forward and the surfaces facing rearward, so small pressure errors show up in it.
drag.line.caption: Pressure drag {symbol}
drag.facing.caption: This car’s predicted pressure drag, split by which way the surface faces
drag.learners.caption: Cross-validated drag error, in counts (one count is {count})
